items.titleIt: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti

items.title: Uganda: 3.6 Million Ugandans Face Acute Food Insecurity As Crisis Threatens to Worsen
items.description: [Nile Post] About 3.6 million Ugandans are facing high levels of acute food insecurity, with the number projected to rise to 4.4 million between February and June 2027, according to the 2026 Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Report on Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition.

items.title: Ethiopia: Moyale Clashes Leave Trail of Death, Destruction Across Seven Districts - Tens of Thousands Flee to Kenya
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Fighting triggered by a dispute over the display of the Somali regional state flag in border city Moyale, a city administered by both Oromia and Somali regions, has spread across seven districts over the weekend, leaving a trail of deaths, injuries and property destruction. Tens of thousands have also fled across the border into Kenya seeking safety.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Moyale Clashes Leave Trail of Death, Destruction Across Seven Districts - Tens of Thousands Flee to Kenya

items.title: Somalia's Eritrean-trained naval chief appointment risks further straining ties with Ethiopia
items.description: Mohamed Abdulqadir "Shariif" has been appointed commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defence Forces, replacing Brig. Gen. Abdiwahab Omar. His military training in Eritrea comes at a sensitive time for the region, with relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea deteriorating and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raising fears of a wider confrontation.  The appointment could cause concern in Addis Ababa, particularly as Somalia has strengthened its engagement with Eritrea and Egypt amid longstanding disputes with Ethiopia over sovereignty, regional security and access to the Red Sea.
